title: Repo Heirloom Time Capsule
oneLiner: A playful physical-ownership kit that turns a beloved GitHub repo into a printable archive, story card, and handoff ritual.
targetUser: Indie developers, educators, open-source maintainers, and portfolio builders who want to make code feel tangible.
keyUx: Paste repo metadata, choose a preservation mood, then generate a mock CD label, story card, dependency tombstone, and handoff note.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web prototype for "Repo Heirloom Time Capsule". Target user: indie developers and open-source maintainers who want to turn a meaningful repository into a tangible portfolio artifact. Core UX: the user pastes repo metadata, picks an archive mood, and the product generates a mock CD label, dependency tombstone, project story card, and handoff note for future collaborators. Required sections: repo import card, archive mood selector, physical label preview, dependency tombstone, story card editor, and share/export ritual. Use the playful-experimental design profile: memorable concept-forward composition, one bold accent, strong first impression, recognizable controls, and novelty that never hides the workflow.

sourceSignals.source: PC Gamer report on GitHub's limited repo CD-ROM promotion
sourceSignals.evidence: A playful campaign around physical code ownership points to broader anxiety about digital impermanence and archival rituals.
sourceSignals.action: Developers share, preserve, and mythologize projects beyond normal GitHub links.
